articles.title: Indiana football QB Josh Hoover’s ‘dog mentality’ gives Hoosiers a winning edge
articles.summary: Days later, Indiana football QB Josh Hoover's teammates still praising his toughness after 'super special' Michigan win:
articles.body:
BLOOMINGTON — Indiana football's locker room erupted in cheers at Michigan Stadium when coach Curt Cignetti called out Josh Hoover's name.

After every win, Cignetti hand picks top performers to sing the team's fight song. He saved his starting quarterback's name for last in the wake of an emotional 13-6 overtime win over Michigan.

They all let Hoover know how much they appreciated his effort.

While the No. 4 Hoosiers (7-1, 4-1 Big Ten) didn't need another remainder of Hoover's toughness, they got one anyway.

Hoover battled through an undisclosed injury to his throwing arm to help IU pull out its first victory at Michigan Stadium in 59 years . Indiana players first described seeing Hoover's "warrior spirit" back in the season opener against North Texas when he finished off a drive with blood pouring down his face.

While Cignetti considered a quarterback change in the second half , Hoover's teammates never expected him to come out of the game. Indiana players were still singing Hoover's praises days after the game.

"It's the dog mentality," Indiana center Bray Lynch said on Tuesday night. "And if you asked me if he were to get hurt before the season started and played, I would have told you, hell yeah, he would have. He's a dog like that."

Lynch also expected the TCU transfer to eventually come through with a winning play.

Hoover shrugged off a poorly timed second half interception by throwing a dart across the middle to open overtime. His 21-yard completion — IU's longest gain of the afternoon — to tight end Brock Schott set up a go-ahead score.

On the next snap, Hoover fought through a would-be tackler at the goal line for the 4-yard rushing touchdown.

"You saw it in spring ball, you see it in the weight room, and you see it now on Saturdays," Lynch said. "And we have full confidence in him, and we knew that when the time arose to make a play, he was gonna find a way to get done."

The post-game celebration that followed highlighted the importance of Hoover's contributions.

"It's never easy, and you'll see all the stuff online about this and that," Lynch said. "But in that locker room over there, you got a bunch of guys that have sacrificed so much to be where they're at, and done so much in their life to be able to play in games like that, in a stadium like that. I think pulling out a victory like that is super special, it's not easy to win in the Big Ten."

Michael Niziolek is the Indiana beat reporter for The Bloomington Herald-Times. You can follow him on X @michaelniziolek .

articles.title: NBA: Portland Blazers prevail in battle of unbeatens against LA Lakers
articles.summary: Portland beat Lakers, while Jayson Tatum lifts Celtics over Nets and Knicks avert 0-4 start with win against Pistons.
articles.body:
Deni Avdija registered 23 points and nine assists and Ja Morant also scored 23 points to help the balanced Portland Trail Blazers post a 136-129 victory over the host Los Angeles Lakers.

Jrue Holiday added 22 points off the bench and Damian Lillard notched 21 points as Portland won its third straight game to open the season on Tuesday night.

Robert Williams III had 14 points and 10 rebounds and Toumani Camara added 12 points for Portland. Avdija, Lillard and Camara each drained four 3-pointers as the Trail Blazers hit 18 of 36 from behind the arc.

Luka Doncic recorded 41 points and nine assists for the Lakers two days after he scored 52 points against the Utah Jazz. Austin Reaves added 26 points and seven assists as Los Angeles lost for the first time in four games.

Sandro Mamukelashvili scored 17 points, Walker Kessler had 13 and Ziaire Williams put up 11 for the Lakers, who shot 56.2 percent from the field and made 17 of 43 (39.5 percent) from 3-point range. Doncic shot 6 of 15 from long range, and Reaves was 4 of 8.

Portland shot 59 percent overall. Donovan Clingan finished with nine points and 10 rebounds for the Trail Blazers.

Portland led 128-124 after Avdija connected on a trey with 2:59 remaining. Williams hit a trey for the Lakers 23 seconds later to make it a one-point margin.

Morant’s floater gave the Trail Blazers a 130-127 edge with 2:01 left. Morant hit another shot with 1:24 to play before Doncic answered with a short shot to cut Los Angeles’ deficit back to three with 1:06 remaining.

Lillard then buried a 3-pointer to give Portland a 135-129 lead with 43.1 seconds left.

Doncic and Reaves both missed 3-point attempts on the next Lakers’ possession, and Holiday later split two free throws to make it a seven-point lead with 18.3 seconds left as Portland closed it out.

Mamukelashvili made two 3-pointers during a 7-0 run to close the first half and Reaves and Doncic opened the second with treys to give the Lakers a 79-68 advantage.

Los Angeles later led 97-88 after a 3-pointer by Reaves and a basket by Doncic before the Trail Blazers scored 14 of the final 20 points in the period to trail 103-102 entering the fourth quarter.

Lillard drilled a 3-pointer to give Portland a 108-105 lead with 9:10 remaining in the game. A trey by Camara increased the gap to 114-106 with 8:31 to play.

Los Angeles answered with a 10-2 spurt. Reaves’ jumper ended the run and tied the game at 116 with 5:33 left.

Doncic scored 24 points in the first half as the Lakers led 73-68. Morant had 15 first-half points for the Trail Blazers.

Tatum’s OT buzzer-beater lifts Celtics over Nets

Jayson Tatum made an elbow ‌jumper as time expired in overtime to give the Boston Celtics ⁠a 125-124 victory ⁠over the visiting Brooklyn Nets.

Tatum scored a game-high 40 points and hit a career-high 18 free throws on ⁠22 attempts. Paul George added 20 points, seven rebounds and seven assists for Boston, which won its third game in a row.

Michael Porter Jr amassed ⁠27 points and 12 rebounds for the Nets, who fell to 0-4. Julius Randle finished with 24 points and nine rebounds.

Brooklyn trailed 117-114 late in the fourth quarter, but Mikel Brown Jr sent the game to overtime by making ‌a 3-pointer with one second left.

Knicks avert 0-4 start with victory over Pistons

Karl-Anthony Towns scored 13 of his game-high 27 points during a decisive third-quarter run as host New York rallied past Detroit for its first win of the season.

The Knicks outscored the Pistons 37-13 in the third and held off a fourth-quarter rally to avoid becoming the first defending NBA ⁠champion to open 0-4 since the Boston Celtics in 1969-70. ⁠Towns also pulled down a season-high 20 rebounds, while Jalen Brunson produced 23 points and seven assists.

Paul Reed had 22 points and nine rebounds for the Pistons, who were seeking their ⁠first 4-0 start since the 2018-19 season. Cade Cunningham totalled 19 points, nine rebounds and eight assists.

Spurs nearly flawless in 80-point first half, keep Kings winless

Victor Wembanyama poured in 29 points ⁠and grabbed 10 rebounds in just 27 minutes, and Julian Champagnie canned eight first-half 3-pointers as host San Antonio steamrolled Sacramento.

San Antonio set league season highs for points (80), assists (23) and 3-pointers (13) in a ‌half in a near-complete performance before the break. Champagnie finished with 26 points as the Spurs won their second game in a row.

De’Andre Hunter put ‌up ‌24 points for the Kings, who dropped to 0-4 on the season. Zach LaVine added 22, and Domantas Sabonis amassed 20 points, 14 rebounds and eight assists.

articles.title: Breaking down the schedule for Week 10 of SCAC football
articles.summary: The final week of the regular season for high school football is here. Check out previews for the top SCAC games going on this week.
articles.body:
It's finally here. Week 10 has arrived and the final push before the District 3 playoffs begin in earnest begins now.

A handful of teams have all but locked in their postseason spots. A handful still sit on the bubble. In Class 4A, West York and Hanover refuse to budge from their perches atop the District 3 power rankings as two of the three remaining undefeated teams in the entire district.

Week 10 is when it everything gets hectic. Who gets another week? Who can finish out strong? Who has to fight to keep the postseason pipe dream alive?

Check out the previews for the top games going on around the SCAC in Week 10, as well as the complete weekend schedule for the league.

Spring Grove (7-2, 4-1 Division I) at South Western (6-3, 3-2 Division I)

The Rockets roll on to another week. They've put up three straight games with four touchdowns in wins over Red Lion, York High and Dallastown, right on the heels of their 51-14 win over New Oxford back in Week 6. Since the Rockets have gone on their four-game win streak, running back Brody Redding has put down 597 rushing yards and six touchdowns, putting him well within reach of cracking 1,000 yards before the postseason.

On the flip side, South Western has gone on its own four-game win streak, bolstered by back-to-back 17-14 wins over York High and New Oxford. Their defensive presence has carried them through the past four weeks, with players like Kyran Nock and Colton Cassetta coming up big against York High.

West York (9-0, 6-0 Division II) at Dover (8-1, 6-0 Division II)

The big one. Both teams have been building to this game all season. West York hasn't given up more than 14 points to a division opponent all season and hasn't been held under 40 points since Week 2 against Red Lion. The Bulldogs have had everything fall their way thus far, and they've held onto the lead for the Division II crown since they entered Week 4.

Still, Dover has only improved since they've gone along. They're fully intent on not repeating the same mistakes that cut them down Week 1 against Conestoga Valley. Their own offense has scored more than 40 points in four games this season, and they haven't given up more than 17 points to any SCAC team, Division II or otherwise.

Either way, the Division II crown gets handed off this week. No split winner, no shares. Winner takes it all.

Littlestown (7-2, 5-1 Division III) at Big Spring (8-1, 5-1 Division III)

Despite everything, the Division III crown is still partially in play this week. Whoever comes out on top between the Bulldogs and Bolts can potentially hold a share of the Division III title should Hanover fall to James Buchanan — the Rockets are 0-6 in division play this year.

Big Spring still has one of the most potent offenses in the league. Even if they were held scoreless in the second half last week, the Bulldogs were still in the game until the final minutes. Plus, they survived a defensive battle with Delone Catholic and dropped at least 40 points on three other division rivals.

Littlestown, meanwhile, took Hanover to overtime and only fell because of a final two-point conversion. Since then, it has won three straight and averaged over 31 points per game in that span. In fact, it's scored at least 30 points in each of its wins and has only been held under that margin twice — a 14-10 loss to Susquehannock and the overtime duel with Hanover.

articles.title: Gaylord-area teams get a fresh start as volleyball districts begin
articles.summary: Gaylord, JoBurg and St. Mary open volleyball districts Nov. 2. See each team's schedule, outlook and our picks to win their brackets.
articles.body:
GAYLORD — One of the benefits of the MHSAA volleyball playoffs is that, regardless of how your team performed in August, September and October, the postseason gives every team a chance to turn an ordinary season into a championship season in November.

Both Gaylord and St. Mary are hoping to do just that when districts begin on Monday, Nov. 2, after finishing the regular season with under 10 wins each. Meanwhile, Johannesburg-Lewiston finished another regular season with at least 25 wins, but faces a tough Division 3 district bracket without its best player, senior Mady Peppin.

When and where will Gaylord area volleyball teams be playing next week, and who has the best chance of winning a district title?

Gaylord (Division 1, District 1; Non-traditional host)

Semifinals, Monday, Nov. 2: Marquette vs. Alpena, 5 p.m., at Marquette; Petoskey vs. Gaylord , 6 p.m., at Gaylord

Finals, 6 p.m., Thursday, Nov. 5 at Gaylord

Outlook: Gaylord volleyball's regular season has been more about reestablishing a culture within the program than chasing wins and losses. Even still, this bracket may be the most favorable district bracket a team like Gaylord could ask for.

Even with two losses to Petoskey on its record, the Blue Devils have played the Northmen to at least four sets in each of the two regular season matchups. If Gaylord can find its way past its rival in round one, the Blue Devils would host a match against Alpena, another team they played to five sets, or Marquette, a 10-win team that would have to travel nearly four hours across the bridge to Jim Mongeau Gymnasium.

While still not the most likely outcome, a district title isn't out of the question for GHS this season.

Prediction: Marquette def. Petoskey in finals

Johannesburg-Lewiston (Division 3, District 68; Mancelona)

First round, Monday, Nov. 2: Mancelona vs. Grand Traverse Academy, 5:30 p.m.; JoBurg vs. Glen Lake, 7 p.m.

Semifinals, Wednesday, Nov. 4: Traverse City St. Francis vs. Mancy/GTA, 5:30 p.m.; Elk Rapids vs. JL /Glen Lake, 7 p.m.

Finals, Thursday, Nov. 5 at Mancelona High School

Outlook : JoBurg volleyball has been as consistent as any program in Northern Michigan, consistently turning in winning records at the end of the regular season while being a staple in the Ski Valley Conference hunt. This may be head coach Kristine Peppin's best coaching job to date, however, finishing with over 25 wins again despite losing her best player, Mady Peppin, on the first day of the regular season.

Still, a more favorable district draw would have been nice.

Traverse City St. Francis is the clear favorite to win this district, ranked No. 6 in the state for Division 3 and a state title contender. Elk Rapids could also compete with TCSF, an honorable mention in the Division 3 rankings and the last program to beat St. Francis in a district matchup back in 2022.

Even Glen Lake poses a challenge for the Cardinals in the first round, a team with wins over Onekama and Charlevoix on its 2026 resume.

Prediction: TCSF def. Elk Rapids in finals

Gaylord St. Mary (Division 4, District 105; St. Mary)

First round, Monday, Nov. 2: Gaylord St. Mary vs. Wolverine, 5:30 p.m.

Semifinals, Wednesday, Nov. 4: Boyne Falls vs. GSM /Wolverine, 5:30 p.m.; East Jordan vs. Ellsworth, 7 p.m.

Finals, Thursday, Nov. 5 at Gaylord St. Mary

Outlook: Can Gaylord St. Mary put a tough regular season behind it? If they want to do that, the Snowbirds will have to go through a tough district bracket in their home gym.

Boyne Falls and East Jordan seem to be the favorites to make it to the district finals, while GSM will need to find a way past Wolverine and Boyne Falls to reach the final match of the bracket.

GSM has a young roster, featuring just one senior and two juniors. District titles may be in GSM's future, but it's tough to see the trophy staying in Gaylord this season.

Prediction: East Jordan def. Boyne Falls in finals

articles.title: Enduring memories and 'imposter syndrome' - The GAA Social meets Mayo star Carney
articles.summary: The GAA Social returns for an in-depth interview with Mayo All-Ireland winner and Footballer of the Year nominee Jack Carney.
articles.body:
Jack Carney has two enduring memories from the whirlwind of celebrations that followed Mayo's return to the promised land after 75 years.

Both are linked to places that helped shape him.

He will never forget seeing the crowd of people that waited at Kilmeena - his home club - to see their heroes bring Sam Maguire onto their patch.

Kilmeena was the last stop on the All-Ireland champions' homecoming parade, as Andy Moran's side were roared

Running behind schedule, when the bus finally arrived, Carney was struck by the numbers that stuck around to see one of their own.

"To see the amount of people that waited there just to see the team, to see Sam Maguire returning to such a small club, no-one ever thought it was possible," Carney tells Thomas Niblock and Oisin McConville on the GAA Social.

"To finally bring it back there to my local people was something I'll never forget."

The other memory Carney hopes proves ineradicable is the powerful feeling that accompanied carrying Sam onto Achill Island alongside team-mates Donnacha McHugh and Diarmuid O'Connor.

Carney has deep family roots on the island. His father and grandfather hail from there and both were present as Carney, McHugh and O'Connor - soundtracked by more than 100 bagpipers, including his father - carried the famous trophy across the Michael Davitt Bridge and onto the island.

Given his connection to Achill, the power and significance of the moment was not lost on Carney.

"According to my father and grandfather, that's never happened before [bringing Sam Maguire on to the island], so I recognised the cultural importance of it - and you could feel it," says Carney.

"That originally wasn't on the calendar as a club until further down the line. The island empties when summer is over. People return to where they're from originally, Dublin or Galway or wherever, and I really wanted to get the trophy down there while the island was vibrant and alive.

"My grandfather was the sergeant on Achill Island. My father grew up in the barracks and the GAA pitch was the back garden. They kind of claim me as half one of their own."

Carney, whose two-point score launched Mayo's All-Ireland final comeback against Kerry, added: "With no Achill player on the team, it was really important that both myself and Donnacha - both our fathers are from there - to get down there and show our appreciation for what they've done for us and our families.

"And Diarmuid O'Connor just has a sense of knowing when something will be good and when to be there.

"He came down with us and I'm delighted he was there because someone who didn't really understand the weight of it all - when we were crossing the bridge, he could say he could just feel it, he said, 'this is something different here'."

Carney's journey to clutching Sam on a sun-kissed evening on Achill Island bears repeating.

He made his inter-county debut in 2021, and while he didn't make the squad for that year's All-Ireland final loss to Tyrone, he delivered a man-of-the-match display in another Croke Park decider a few months later to help Kilmeena win the All-Ireland Junior Club title.

It wasn't long before Carney became a Mayo regular. He featured under James Horan and Kevin McStay but found a new level thanks to Andy Moran's leadership and became a key cog in the run to the All-Ireland title.

He has also benefited from the new rules, establishing himself as a deadly two-point marksman in the green and red. He nailed two of them in the All-Ireland final win over Kerry amid an all-action display that helped his county end a 75-year wait.

While acquiring a knack for raising orange flags hasn't hurt his cause, it was Carney's all-round contributions that sealed a Footballer of the Year nomination alongside team-mate Ryan O'Donoghue and Kerry star David Clifford.

"There's a bit of imposter syndrome to be mentioned alongside those two boys," admits Carney.

"I genuinely suffer from feeling a little less worthy than Ryan and David because of what they do on the big stage time after time.

"But I'm very glad the work I've done in the last 17 or 18 years has come to fruition. Not for me, but for my family and my club, the first player from Kilmeena to be nominated as an All-Star."

Whether or not Carney follows Moran and Lee Keegan to become Mayo's third footballer of the year, the 25-year-old will be instrumental in the county's All-Ireland defence in 2027.

"After the All-Stars [on Friday], we go to Barbados the next morning for 10 days," he said.

"The timing of that is great for the group because when you come back there's a bookmark in the 2026 season and we move on from there.

"That's the time our mindset will shift to 2027. We're a young group, we're ambitious. The celebrations can't go on forever."

articles.title: What is the Rutgers quarterback situation entering Michigan game?
articles.summary: Rutgers starting quarterback Dylan Lonergan suffered an injury in the previous game. Will be play vs. Michigan?
articles.body:
PISCATAWAY – In a season filled with quarterback questions, now Rutgers football is facing another .

Who will start this week's game against Michigan?

That's the newest question and it's relevant after starter Dylan Lonergan suffered an injury early in the Scarlet Knights ' 42-14 loss to Northwestern on Oct. 24, and whether he'll be able to play remains unclear.

Schiano said Tuesday, Oct. 27 that he will leave Lonergan's status to the availability report, the first of which is released Wednesday night.

It was the second game this season that Lonergan had to leave because of an injury – he also missed the team's game against Boston College (the second game of the season) because of the injury he suffered in Week 1 in the loss to UMass.

It's been a disappointing campaign so far for Lonergan, who was showing signs of improvement and played his best game as a Scarlet Knight in the Oct. 17 win over Maryland.

"I'm disappointed and sad for the kid because this means so much to him and he puts so much of himself into it," Schiano said. "To have to leave the game now for the (second) time, yeah it's killing him. And I'm sad for us because he really was coming on. You could see it against (Southern California) and you could see it at Maryland. You could see him really coming on. Injuries are part of football. It's a violent game."

If Lonergan can't play, then Rutgers has to look to AJ Surace or Sean Ashenfelder.

Surace again struggled after coming in for Lonergan, going just 7-of-18 passing for 64 yards with one interception against Northwestern.

Seeking a spark in the second half, Schiano called on third-stringer Sean Ashenfelder, who went 2-of-9 for 36 yards.

Ashenfelder hasn't even gotten many practice reps, partially because the bulk of them in even in training camp went to Lonergan and Surace as they battled for the job. Schiano reiterated again Tuesday that once the season starts, there are even fewer reps to go around.

Surace is in his third year with the program and he just hasn't played well enough in the chances he's gotten so far this season.

Schiano, though, has liked how Surace has battled through the adversity. He's still confident in Surace's ability.

"AJ's a fighter," Schiano said. "He's not happy with the way he's played. But he came out in practice like the national championship's around the corner. That's the way he approaches everything he does. If you're going to bet on a guy, probably bet on him."

articles.title: Sharks Locker Room: San Jose Playing “Easy Way”, Trouba Gets “A”, Celebrini Real About Splitting WillMack
articles.summary: San Jose Sharks head coach Ryan Warsofsky seemed happy with just one player in Tuesday’s 2-0 loss to the Buffalo […]
articles.body:
San Jose Sharks head coach Ryan Warsofsky seemed happy with just one player in Tuesday's 2-0 loss to the Buffalo Sabres.

"You want it the easy way," Warsofsky said, of the Sharks getting outshot 40-23. "It's not the easy way in the National Hockey League."

Besides Yaroslav Askarov stopping 38-of-39 shots, the Sharks just didn't generate enough 5-on-5 offense once again, and their piping-hot power play, 5-of-11 in their last three games, went cold.

After the game, Warsofsky spoke more about his displeasure in his team's performance, Macklin Celebrini discussed playing away from Will Smith , Jacob Trouba talked about getting the "A" in Alex Wennberg 's absence, and Michael Kesselring was candid about his first game against his ex-team.

A deeper game story with micro-stats from Stathletes and game action clips, Sharks Insight, will be published soon.

Warsofsky, on what's missing for the San Jose Sharks right now:

You got to get comfortable being uncomfortable. I think that's the biggest thing. You want it the easy way. It's not the easy way in the National Hockey League. It's hard. It's demanding. It's every shift. It's every period. It's every day. It's practice. It's games. We need to work on being a little bit more competitive all over the ice.

Warsofsky, on all the stretch passes that the Sharks tried tonight:

We're looking for home runs. We got to learn to play small ball, and then, those [stretch passes] will happen, naturally. It's like every shift there, especially early in the game. We're looking for a lot of home runs, and it's just not the way you win in this league.

Warsofsky, on Yaroslav Askarov's performance:

He was good, really good tonight. Gave us a chance. We need to lessen his workload. That's for sure. But nice to see him, he's locked in.

Celebrini, on WillMack getting separated:

Reality was, we weren't really creating much. Or, we weren't scoring. When things aren't working, you got to switch it up a little bit. I think it's nothing really to read too much into. I think [it was] just a decision that was made to just try something new and shake it up. He's a great player. That line can create as many chances as anyone.

Celebrini, on the San Jose Sharks' failed stretch passes:

It's tough. I mean, some of those plays, if it gets through, then it's a great play. But if it doesn't work, then you're kicking yourself.

Trouba, on the San Jose Sharks' failed stretch passes:

I don't think you want to get too spaced out. Maybe every once in a while, you'll catch one of those but wouldn't say it's a high percentage way to sustain offense.

That'd be a good idea [to break out closer together].

It was hard in the first. It was pretty emotional, honestly, for me tonight. I thought in the second and third, I really started to get it going. Obviously, personally, I wanted to show that they made a mistake, but we didn't win, and that's what really matters.

articles.title: ITV: estos son los tres grandes defectos por los que suspenden los coches de más de 15 años
articles.standfirst: La edad media de los coches en nuestro país supera ya los 15 años, y a esa edad los coches tienen ya muchas posibilidades de caer en la ITV por defectos en tres áreas principales
articles.summary: La edad media de los coches en nuestro país supera ya los 15 años, y a esa edad los coches tienen ya muchas posibilidades de caer en la ITV por defectos en tres áreas principales
articles.body: Un coche con más de 15 años no tiene por qué dar problemas en la ITV. Pero el paso del tiempo deja huella, y no siempre donde uno espera. A veces basta con una bombilla fundida; otras, el desgaste está en componentes que no se ven a simple vista pero que son responsables de que el coche vaya por su sitio (la seguridad, ya sabes). Según los datos analizados por la Asociación Española de Entidades Colaboradoras de la Administración en la Inspección Técnica de Vehículos (AECA-ITV), casi dos de cada tres defectos graves detectados en estos coches se concentran en los tres apartados que te vamos a desvelar. Y no debemos descuidarlos porque en España los vehículos tienen ya una antigüedad media de 15,2 años. En este contexto, y aunque un coche bien cuidado puede seguir circulando durante mucho tiempo (otra cuestión es que las restricciones medioambientales impidan su uso en determinadas zonas), conviene prestar atención a estos tres elementos, que son los que antes tienen posibilidades de fallar. El alumbrado y la señalización encabezan la lista de suspensos en la ITV, con el 23,1% de los defectos graves detectados en coches de más de 15 años. Aquí entran desde las bombillas fundidas hasta los fallos en cables o fusibles. Más allá de que una luz fundida reduzca la visibilidad, también dificulta que los demás conductores nos vean o sepan qué vamos a hacer (si lo que falla es un intermitente, por ejemplo). Y algunos de estos fallos solo los conocemos cuando llega el momento de pasar la inspección, pese a que se pueden comprobar en el garaje o la calle en apenas unos minutos antes de ir a pasar la inspección. El segundo gran punto negro son las emisiones contaminantes, responsables del 22,3% de los defectos graves. En este caso, el problema puede estar en piezas como el catalizador, el filtro de partículas o la válvula EGR, que con el tiempo pueden deteriorarse y dejar de cumplir correctamente su función. Está claro que esto no es algo que se pueda comprobar como se comprueban las luces. Y, aunque tratemos de investigarlo, no siempre hay una señal evidente de que algo va mal. El coche puede seguir funcionando con aparente normalidad y superar los límites de emisiones establecidos para la inspección. Lo malo es que cuando alguno de estos elementos falla, la reparación puede salir bastante más cara que una revisión preventiva. No todos los coches antiguos tienen por qué contaminar más de la cuenta, pero sí conviene no ignorar los avisos del coche ni dejar pasar revisiones cuando hay indicios de un problema mecánico. Por ejemplo, cuando notamos alguien nos avisa o advertimos por el espejo retrovisor que el coche echa más humo de lo habitual. El tercer apartado reúne los defectos en ejes, ruedas, neumáticos y suspensión, que representan el 20,1% del total de suspensos en coches de 15 años o más. Aquí el desgaste afecta al comportamiento del coche, porque unos neumáticos en mal estado ofrecen menos adherencia y unos amortiguadores deteriorados perjudican la estabilidad y (no menos importante) aumentan la distancia de frenado. Estos son elementos que sufren con los kilómetros y los baches. Además, no siempre basta con echar un vistazo rápido a las ruedas para saber si todo está en orden. Conviene comprobar el estado y el desgaste de los neumáticos y prestar atención a síntomas como una pérdida de estabilidad o un comportamiento extraño al pasar por baches. Los frenos también merecen atención, aunque quedan fuera de esos tres primeros puestos de causas de suspenso: concentran el 11,4% de los defectos graves. Discos, pastillas y otros componentes pueden perder eficacia con el uso, y su estado resulta decisivo cuando hay que detener el coche ante un imprevisto. La importancia de estas revisiones va más allá de conseguir la pegatina de la ITV. Según un estudio de la Fundación Línea Directa, los turismos de 15 años o más concentran el 42,9% de los vehículos con fallos implicados en accidentes con víctimas. En los coches de hasta cuatro años, la proporción es solo del 16%. De todas formas, conviene ser justos y reconocer que tener un coche antiguo no significa de forma obligatoria tener un coche inseguro. El estado de conservación y el mantenimiento cuentan, y mucho. El problema aparece cuando los pequeños fallos se dejan pasar ("no me voy a gastar un euro, que ya es viejo", dicen muchos conductores) hasta el punto de que se convierten en averías que nos pueden provocar un accidente. La recomendación, por tanto, es bastante sencilla: no esperar a que llegue la fecha de la ITV para comprobar cómo está el coche. Revisar las luces, vigilar los neumáticos y atender los avisos mecánicos son gestos que pueden ahorrar tiempo y dinero, además de ayudar a evitar riesgos.

articles.title: Arteta insists attitude not to blame as Arsenal exit Carabao Cup to Fleetwood
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta has insisted he "cannot fault" the attitude of his Arsenal players after a Carabao Cup fourth-round defeat on penalties to Fleetwood Town.The Le...
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta has insisted he "cannot fault" the attitude of his Arsenal players after a Carabao Cup fourth-round defeat on penalties to Fleetwood Town.

The League Two side, who sit 18th in the fourth tier, knocked out last season's finalists after a shoot-out on Tuesday night.

Fleetwood arrived as specialists from the spot. According to Opta , they have now won their last four penalty shoot-outs in all competitions, converting each of their last 16 spot-kicks across those shoot-outs.

Before the game, Arteta had warned that Arsenal could not drop their standards if they were to avoid an upset, but saw his side crash out of the competition in a huge upset.

Speaking after the final whistle, Arteta congratulated the hosts and defended his squad's effort.

"Congrats to Fleetwood, it's a sad day for us. But I cannot fault at all the attitude of the players. I haven't seen anybody not doing what is required at this level."

The Arsenal manager also declined to give an immediate verdict on the red card shown to Max Dowman during the tie. The 16-year-old was sent off after reacting to a robust from Fleetwood midfielder Harrison Neal. Dowman thrust a knee at Neal, who had slid in on the teenager on the touchline.

"Max Dowman's red card? I prefer to watch it back properly, and then I can assess the situation. We learn from everything."

Arteta pointed to Arsenal's dominance of the ball and the volume of chances they created as evidence that his side had done enough to progress on another night.

"We insisted so much, we had so much of the ball, so many chances, so many shots. This is football.

Arsenal's exit continues a poor record in the League Cup

articles.title: Lakers can’t get stops, suffer first loss of season
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES — The Lakers kept finding ways to score.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES — The Lakers kept finding ways to score. Finding enough stops proved more difficult.

Luka Doncic's 41 points couldn't prevent Los Angeles' first loss of the season Tuesday night, dropping to 3-1 after a 136-129 loss to the Portland Trail Blazers at Crypto.com Arena.

Portland had four players score more than 20 points. Ja Morant and Deni Avdija finished with 23 apiece, Jrue Holiday added 22 off the bench and Damian Lillard scored 21, including a sidestep 3-pointer with 43 seconds remaining that iced the game and push their undefeated record alive to 3-0.

Their balanced production, combined with fouls and defensive breakdowns, kept the Lakers from sustaining momentum.

"We got broken down a lot," Lakers coach JJ Redick said. "The game plan discipline, KYP personnel discipline wasn't where it needs to be."

Austin Reaves contributed 26 points and seven assists, and Sandro Mamukelashvili added 17 points for L.A.

The Lakers committed 16 first-half fouls, giving the Trail Blazers 21 free-throw attempts before halftime. L.A. ended the night with 29 fouls that gave Portland 41 attempts (made 26) at the free throw line.

Flopping calls added to the interruptions, disrupting the Lakers' rhythm as they tried to build on an efficient offensive start.

L.A. shot better than 56% from the field, but Portland shot 59% and made 18 of 36 3-point attempts.

"If we score 129 points at home, we should be able to get enough stops to win," Redick said.

The Lakers opened by making five of their first six shots for a 14-7 lead. Doncic scored 16 first-quarter points, including two 3-pointers, helping L.A. take a 38-32 advantage.

Portland stayed close by making 10 of 14 shots in the period, then opened the second quarter with a 26-16 run.

As the Lakers' foul total climbed, the Trail Blazers repeatedly reached the line, preventing L.A. from establishing a sustained run.

Mamukelashvili provided a lift with a buzzer-beating 3-pointer that sent the Lakers into halftime ahead 73-68. Doncic had 24 points, while Reaves added 14 points, five rebounds and four assists.

Portland changed the momentum and erased any Lakers lead or momentum in the second half, outscoring the L.A. 68-56.

"We still have to be mindful of turnovers," Reaves said. "But yeah, offense has been good."

Portland's fourth-quarter zone presented another challenge. Redick said the Lakers generated open shots, but they couldn't consistently follow those possessions with stops.

L.A. cut the deficit to 114-112 as defensive chants grew louder. Portland answered, with Lillard eventually delivering the decisive shot.

"We had a lot of blown assignments," Reaves said. "It was everybody, it wasn't just one person."

Walker Kessler pointed to breakdowns against penetration and ball screens.

"I pride myself on being the leader on the defense and I didn't perform tonight," Kessler said.

The Lakers face the Clippers on Wednesday in the second game of a back-to-back.

"Tonight we lost, but we got another opportunity tomorrow night to go get a win," Reaves said.

articles.title: JJ Redick: Lakers lacked defensive discipline during Tuesday's loss
articles.summary: Lakers coach JJ Redick commented on his team's defensive shortcomings in Tuesday's loss to the Trail Blazers.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers suffered their first loss of the new NBA season on Tuesday to the Portland Trail Blazers , and the way they lost wasn't too surprising. They scored 129 points on 56.3% field-goal shooting, but they allowed Portland to make 59% of its shot attempts, resulting in a seven-point defeat .

Portland came out on top in this game thanks largely to its outside shooting. It made seven 3-pointers in the fourth quarter, and its three main guards -- Ja Morant, Damien Lillard and Jrue Holiday -- all did lots of damage, as the three men scored over 20 points apiece and 66 points combined.

Defense, especially perimeter defense, was a big focus for the Lakers coming into the regular season. Coach JJ Redick said that their defensive discipline wasn't there during Tuesday's game.

"We just got broken down a lot," Redick said. "I thought the game plan discipline, KYP (know your personnel), personnel discipline wasn't where it needs to be, and I think sometimes early in the season these are good learning lessons that we can all apply, both as coaches and as players."

At this point of the season, games such as this one can serve more as information than as a red flag, especially when it comes to defense. Certain minutiae within the Lakers' defensive strategy will need to be tweaked, and of course, the team needs to build chemistry, given that it has nine new players on its roster.

On the other hand, Tuesday's game was also a shootout, and therefore, to a certain extent, it may simply have been a case of the Blazers being able to make more shots down the stretch while the Lakers cooled off considerably after scoring 73 points in the first half and 103 points through three quarters.

The good news for the Lakers is that they will get right back to work on Wednesday against the Los Angeles Clippers, which means that they can right their wrongs quickly and get back on the right track.

articles.title: Xhaka, Embolo return to Swiss squad after fake COVID docs affair
articles.summary: Granit Xhaka and Breel Embolo’s return to Switzerland ‘the right course of action,’ national team director says.
articles.body:
Switzerland captain Granit Xhaka and striker Breel Embolo are available for selection again for next month’s Nations League matches after being sanctioned for using forged COVID-19 certificates during the pandemic, the Swiss Football Association said.

The pair were dropped and missed the first four Nations League games, in September and October.

Sunderland midfielder Xhaka, 34, who holds a Swiss record 152 caps, admitted to using a forged vaccine certificate to avoid mandatory jabs during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Atlanta United forward Embolo, 29, similarly acknowledged that a penal order against him concerned fake COVID certificates.

“The Swiss Football Association (SFV) will once again consider Granit Xhaka and Breel Embolo for the national team, beginning with the Nations League matches in November,” it said in a statement on Tuesday.

“The SFV has thoroughly examined both cases and has concluded that the players’ return is justifiable given the completion of legal proceedings and the sporting consequences incurred [having missed four international matches].”

National team director Pierluigi Tami said: “We are convinced that a return to the national team in November is both responsible and the right course of action.”

Switzerland coach Murat Yakin, his staff and the players’ council unanimously decided that Xhaka will remain the captain.

Switzerland are top of Group B1 in the Nations League, with four straight wins so far.

Yakin will announce his squad for the final two Nations League group matches on November 5. Xhaka and Embolo are on the shortlist, the Swiss FA said.

Switzerland travel to face second-placed Slovenia on November 13, then host Scotland in St Gallen three days later.

“I’m pleased that I can once again make unrestricted selections for the squad in November,” said Yakin.

When the Swiss squad got together in late September, the Lucerne public prosecutor’s office opened an investigation into Xhaka, who admitted obtaining a fake certificate and stepped down.

A few days later, Embolo withdrew from the squad for similar reasons.

Both Xhaka and Embolo were given a suspended fine of 150,000 Swiss francs ($181,225), which will be in place for a probationary period of two years.

The SFV has announced guidelines for handling future matters that involve criminal law.

images.caption: Switzerland's Breel Embolo celebrates scoring the team's first goal with Granit Xhaka [Issei Kato/Reuters]

articles.title: Former world No 3 Stan Wawrinka ends career in home match defeat in Basel
articles.summary: Stan Wawrinka, one of few players to win multiple Grand Slams in era dominated by Federer, Nadal and Djokovic, retires.
articles.body:
Stan Wawrinka bid farewell to tennis as he brought the curtain down on a decorated 24-year career following a first-round exit at the Basel Open on Tuesday.

The 41-year-old Swiss announced earlier in the season that his last tournament as a professional would be the ATP 500-level event in his home country, and a 7-5, 7-6 (7/2) defeat by Czech Jiri Lehecka brought an end to the career of the three-time major champion.

Former world number three Wawrinka, along with Andy Murray, was the only player to win multiple Grand Slams in a period dominated by Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic.

“I was lucky enough to be able to play alongside them and sometimes beat them,” Wawrinka told the AFP news agency in 2024.

He bested Nadal to win his first Grand Slam at the Australian Open in 2014, before beating Djokovic in the French Open final the following season and then again in the US Open title match in 2016.

Alongside his compatriot Federer, the Lausanne native won the Davis Cup for Switzerland and claimed gold in the doubles at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.

On court in Basel, Wawrinka’s every point won, as well as several trademark booming one-handed backhands, was greeted by wild cheers from the partisan home crowd.

But Lehecka got his nose in front with a break of serve in the 11th game and sealed the opening set with an ace.

A tight second set went to a tie-break, but it was just a step too far for Wawrinka as his 21st-ranked opponent took firm control to seal the breaker and the match.

Wawrinka, who enjoyed a farewell ceremony in Basel on Monday, did a lap of the court to thank the crowd before disappearing down the tunnel for the last time.

“He won the biggest tournaments, so for me to be here in his moment is a little bit weird,” Lehecka told Sky Sports.

“But at the same time, it’s a pleasure and I will never forget this match.”

However, fans will have one more chance to see the Swiss in action this year.

Wawrinka announced in June that he will throw a farewell party on December 19 in Geneva, with Federer and Murray also on the card for the “One last backhand” event.

Elsewhere, second seed Arthur Fils beat his fellow Frenchman Giovanni Mpetshi Perricard 7-6 (7/5), 7-5 to reach the round of 16.

Spanish third seed Rafael Jodar cruised past Chilean Alejandro Tabilo in straight sets, while top seed Ben Shelton battled past his American compatriot Aleksandar Kovacevic 6-7 (4/7), 7-6 (7/3), 7-6 (7/4).

Djokovic, who trained with his old friend and foe Wawrinka before the tournament on Sunday, will open his campaign on Wednesday against Ugo Humbert of France.

images.caption: Wawrinka enjoyed a farewell ceremony in Basel on Monday [Claudio Thoma/EPA]

articles.title: London Marathon considering major change to elite women’s race in 2027
articles.summary: The London Marathon CEO Hugh Brasher is open to the idea of a mixed race in 2027 to enable the world’s best women to target the faster, controversial world r...
articles.body:
The London Marathon could allow the elite women's race in 2027 to unfold with male runners and pacemakers in pursuit of faster times and ultimately a world record.

The overall world record, in mixed races, is held by Ruth Chepng'etich (2:09:56), though controversy surrounds that mark set at the 2024 Chicago Marathon after the Kenyan failed a drugs test five months later and was subsequently banned for three years in 2025.

Tigst Assefa, who holds the women only race world record (2:15:41 from London Marathon 2026), appeared on track to break the overall world record at this year's Berlin Marathon before rupturing her Achilles tendon in the closing stages and limping home in 2:11:04.

The distressing scenes left London Marathon CEO Hugh Brasher heartbroken for the Ethiopian athlete and now open to a change that could offer women, including Assefa, should she recover in time, a chance to better Chepng'etich's controversial record in London next year.

"Will London, in the future, have a women's only record? Yes, I think that's important," Brasher, who is pushing for cleaner sport in the World Marathon Majors in light of Peres Jepchirchir's provisional suspension after a failed test , told the Independent . "However, in the past, we've played around with it. Paula [Radcliffe], when she ran 2:15, had the women's only record, so there were men running around her. She probably says they didn't help her at all.

"We're prepared to mix it up. We very much talk to the athletes about what their goals are. I think what Tigst [Assefa] did in Berlin, it was a tragedy, in terms of the injury she got, we wish her well. It was incredible, she was going to beat that world record. It's in touching distance. I'm sorry, but I think that world record is entirely dubious, if you study everything that's been said, from the AIU, and what they believe, that's a personal opinion."

The elite women's race at London has been run as a women-only race in recent years, which usually poses a tougher challenge, given less depth of runners in and around the elite women's time.

However, Paula Radcliffe broke the women's world record in mixed races (2:15:25) in 2003, with Brasher in discussions with the world's best runners over which style of race they would prefer before an announcement on the elite fields expected in January.

"We talk to the women and what they want to achieve, those conversation are still going on about 2027," Brasher added. "We're still signing athletes, and what we will have is some incredible racing, both men and women that are running, when we announce them in January, will have people salivating about racing. They say the London Marathon is harder to win than the Olympics or the World Championships, we delight in the competition and strength of the competition, it's all part of such an incredible day.

"All things are on the table, all things, so many things we're going through, we have ideas."

images.caption: Tigst Assefa ran with male pacemakers in Berlin, with London open to switching its format for 2027 (Getty)
